title: 楚辭集註 (Songs of Chu with Collected Annotations)
shelf_note: Ming woodblock 楚辭集註 with 後語 and 辯證 bound in, as the edition normally is; pages 229 (後語) and 311 (辯證) belong to it.
structure_note: 331 records, 324 with OCR, none translated. The copy carries handwritten marginal comments (蔣云, 洪云, 劉云, 金云, 陳深曰) in the upper margin. reader_summary: This is Zhu Xi's collected commentary on the Chu ci, with the 後語 and 辯證, in a Ming print carrying a reader's handwritten notes. The transcription is of the right text, and the large main text is mostly accurate. But at least one line of main text is dropped, and the handwritten notes are transcribed on one half of a spread and silently left out on the other. There is no English.
book_verdict: Good woodblock OCR with a dropped main-text line on p.146 and inconsistent handling of the manuscript annotations; usable for reading, not for quoting without the image.

structure_note: 292 records, 287 with OCR. The preface (p.10) is cut in cursive script and its OCR is largely wrong; the commentary pages are printed in regular script and read well. The single backstep and repeat probably come from misread leaf numerals.

reader_summary: This is a 1630 sectional exposition of the Book of Documents, not the classic itself. The commentary pages are transcribed accurately enough to read. The cursive preface is badly misread, with one negation reversed. There is no English.
book_verdict: Commentary body is reliable OCR; the cursive preface transcription should not be trusted or quoted.

reader_summary: This is Mao Qiling's topical arrangement of Spring and Autumn entries by rite (court visits, embassies, peace-making, campaigns). The transcription is of the right text and is close to exact, with a misread state name and one garbled note in 4 pages. There is no English.
book_verdict: Clean, well-printed Qing book with accurate OCR; fit to show.

title: 穆天子傳
shelf_note: Chinese woodblock print; it belongs to the shelf. The problem is the title (see structure_note).
structure_note: The record is catalogued as 穆天子傳 (Guo Pu), but none of the 4 sampled pages is from that work. p.19 opens 同昌公主傳 (唐 蘇鶚). p.22 continues it. p.45 is 魏夫人傳 and p.66 is 柳毅傳, each named in its own running title. This is a congshu volume of several tales catalogued under its first item, so a reader searching for these tales will not find them and a reader opening '穆天子傳' meets Tang tales from p.19 on. Catalogue identity class I7.

reader_summary: Under the title 穆天子傳 a reader finds a Ming collection of Tang tales: the Princess Tongchang, Lady Wei, Liu Yi. The transcription of those tales is mostly accurate. But the record does not say what is in it, and none of the sampled pages is the Mu Tianzi zhuan. There is no English.

title: 井觀瑣言 (vol 1)
shelf_note: Ming biji notes, in a Ming congshu print.
structure_note: The volume holds several works. p.27 shows the blank end leaf of 井觀瑣言 facing the opening of 林泉隨筆 (淮浦張綸). p.33 is 林泉隨筆, p.63 is 震澤長語 (王鏊, by running title), and p.95 is another biji with a different running title. The book is catalogued only as 井觀瑣言, so 3 of the 4 sampled pages are other works under its title (I7). The 5 printed repeats and 3 backsteps are what restarting foliation per work produces, not a scan fault.

reader_summary: This is a Ming collection of scholars' notes: 井觀瑣言 followed by 林泉隨筆, 震澤長語 and at least one more work, all filed under the first title. The transcription is accurate and readable. Readers are not told which work they are in, and one page leaks layout arrows. There is no English.
book_verdict: Good OCR; the record needs its contents listed, because most of the volume is not 井觀瑣言.

reader_summary: This is the Jingui yaolue, the Han formulary of Zhang Zhongjing, in a 1598 print, catalogued here with no author. The transcription is of the right text and mostly accurate. But doses and their units are where it slips: one dose is dropped, and 方寸匕 is turned into 'seven'. There is no English.
book_verdict: Readable, but a recipe text whose OCR drops and misreads doses must not be quoted for dosage without the image; the author field should be fixed.

title: 遠鏡說 (On the Telescope)
shelf_note: Schall von Bell's treatise on the telescope; early modern science in Chinese.
structure_note: The scan is the 藝海珠塵 congshu reprint, with 藝海珠塵 in the block margin of every leaf. That collection is Qing (Jiaqing era), but the record gives published 1626, the date of the first edition (I7). 17 records, all with OCR. Show-through from the facing leaf is heavy, and the OCR reads text that is not on the printed face (p.3).

reader_summary: This is Schall von Bell's On the Telescope, in the Qing 藝海珠塵 reprint, not the 1626 first edition the record claims. The running text is transcribed accurately. The pages with diagrams are not: captions are garbled, labels invented, and on p.3 a line naming Ricci as author is invented. There is no English.
book_verdict: Body text is reliable; the plate and diagram pages carry invented text, and the edition date is wrong.
